newsitem.title: USA: Britain's Prince Edward in U.S. TV deal.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Prince Edward in U.S. TV deal.

text.p: Britain's Prince Edward, the queen's youngest son, has sold a series of eight television specials produced by his company to the CBS television network, Variety reported on Tuesday.

The prince, who prefers to be known as Ed Windsor within the TV industry, will host the series which includes the documentary "Edward on Edward," about his great uncle Edward VIII, who abdicated the British throne in 1936.

Windsor made the announcement on Tuesday at the annual conference of the National Association of Television Programme Executives (NATPE) in New Orleans. He spent some time touring the various booths and chatting to delegates, tailed by a discreet security force.

Under the deal, CBS and its Eyemark syndication arm will distribute globally a series of TV specials produced by Ardent Productions, the British-based independent production company co-founded by Windsor.
The prince said this alliance offers his company a significant opportunity in the worldwide TV marketplace.

"This agreement is a landmark in the development of Ardent as a truly international production company," he said. "We are genuinely excited about the prospects for making more high-quality programming and the enthusiasm CBS and Eyemark have shown for our product."
